title: Praxis provenance interchange block (praxis.provenance/1)
description: The versioned, portable form of Praxis provenance that crosses Echelon system boundaries (RQ-ROS-2026-A013..A017, DF-ROS-2026-A037). It carries exactly the contribution history and lineage an artifact carries in front matter (schemas/artifact-provenance.schema.json), tagged with a major version. Receivers MUST preserve unknown fields, MUST carry a block of an unsupported major version verbatim without interpreting it, and MUST reject a malformed block instead of dropping or repairing it. This schema is the structural floor; the conformance fixtures in tests/fixtures/provenance-interchange/ define the full verdicts (including the at-most-one-created, ordering, agent-execution, and credential rules that JSON Schema cannot express). Identity is self-reported provenance: it is not authentication, authorization, or evidence quality.

schema.description: Major version tag. Absent only on the bare front-matter/registry projection, which is read as praxis.provenance/1. A reader that does not support the major version carries the block verbatim.

subject.description: What the block describes, present only on a standalone export (`ros provenance export`). A block embedded in another record describes that record.

contributions.description: Append-only contribution history keyed by execution: EXE-... (a Praxis execution), EXT-<system>.<run-id> (another Echelon system's execution, where <system> is its registry id), or CTB-... (a non-agent contributor outside any execution). An empty object means no provenance is recorded; nothing may be inferred from its absence.

derivedFrom.description: Lineage: what the described record was derived from. Artifact IDs or namespaced foreign references (for example `aegis:fault/F-12`). Lineage is never authorship.

operations.description: Operation codes. Praxis 1.x knows created, modified, reviewed, approved, superseded, migrated, discovered, measured, transformed, remediated, validated, resolved, and x-... extensions. A major-1 reader tolerates, reports, and preserves any other code matching the grammar, because a later 1.x release may add one.
